export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: The claim that the minimizing hitting sets eventually belong to a fixed finite family with bounded products is unsupported; the preceding argument still permits products up to roughly \(a_n/2\), which is unbounded.
grade.summary: The hitting-set formulation and the conditional periodicity argument are useful, but the proof omits the central finiteness argument. It also incorrectly assumes that eventual translation-periodicity can be extended through the initial transient merely by enlarging \(T\) and \(L\).
strengths: Correctly reformulates admissible terms using prime hitting sets and observes the nested nature of these families.
Correctly shows that a recurrence defined by finitely many fixed moduli is translation-equivariant and yields eventual periodic increments.

errors.description: No valid argument establishes an eventual fixed finite collection of relevant hitting sets; this is the central difficulty of the problem.
Eventual equality \(a_{n+T}=a_n+L\) does not automatically imply the required equality for every positive \(n\), and enlarging \(T,L\) does not repair arbitrary initial terms.
The assertion that \(m_n\) is bounded because of the finite set \(P_1\) is not explained, though it can be repaired by noting that \(P_1\) hits every later \(P_i\).
